newsitem.title: USA: Five men settle SEC insider charges.
newsitem.headline: Five men settle SEC insider charges.

text.p: Five men agreed to pay $254,282 to settle insider trading charges involving shares of Royce Laboratories Inc, the Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday.

Without admitting or denying the charges, the five men agreed to repay $128,000 in ill-gotten profits, $51,604.87 in prejudgment interest and $74,677.38 in civil penalites regarding rogue trading of Royce Laboratories stock.

In its September complaint, the agency had alleged the men illegally traded in shares of Miami-based drug manufacturer knowing it was about to or had received tentative approval from federal regulators to market the generic drug Piroxicam.

Two of the men employed with Royce at the time of the complaint are: Nilkanth Patel, 41, of Cooper City, Fla., director of quality assurance and quality control since about 1990, and Hasmukh Patel, 47, of Cooper City, Fla., a chemist with Royce since May 1988.
Hasmukh Patel is still employed with Royce, according to a family member. Nilkanth Patel no longer works there.
The other three are: Janak C. Patel, 39, of Elmhurst, Ill., and his two brothers-in-law: Janak M. Patel, 39, of Wood Dale Ill., and Kanubhai Patel, 43, of Flushing, N.Y.
The commission said the illegal trades took place during the fall of 1991 and spring of 1992.

Another employee involved in the case, Abul Bhuiyan, 43, was not asked to turn over his ill-gotten gains or pay a prejudgment interest because he had forfeited his illegal profits to Royce, the commission said.

However, Bhuiyan, of Miami Springs, Fla., executive vice-president and director of operations of Royce since May 1990, had previously agreed to a $1,811 civil penalty before the commission had filed its civil suit.
Attempts to reach William Nortman, the attorney for Nilkanth Patel and Hasmukh Patel were unsuccessful.
